3	Append only commit log that groups records into durable segments, so a writer publishes a batch atomically and a reader replays exactly the batches that were committed.
4	
5	## Requirements
6	
7	Go 1.22 or newer. Standard library only.
8	
9	## Build
10	
11	    go build ./...
12	    go run ./cmd/logctl --dir <path> stat
13	
14	## Public interface
15	
16	`log.Open(dir string, opts Options) (*Log, error)` opens the log directory. The committed set is taken from a persistent index sidecar (`index.idx`) when it can be adopted incrementally; if it is missing, truncated, version-mismatched, checksum-bad or contradictory to the segments, Open rebuilds it from the segment files, so the index is pure cache and opening a grown log no longer decodes every segment entry. A half-written tail of the last segment (crash mid-write) is discarded without error and its reserved sequence stays a permanent hole; any other inconsistency is `ErrCorruptSegment`.
17	- `(*Log).Append(records [][]byte) (Batch, error)` stages a batch.
18	- `(*Log).Commit(batch Batch) (uint64, error)` makes a batch durable and returns its sequence. The segment entry is synced first, then one index sidecar record; with `Sync`, a failed fsync of either returns `ErrSyncFailed`, both files roll back and the batch stays staged for a retry that never duplicates the entry.
19	- `(*Log).CommitGroup(batches []Batch) ([]uint64, error)` commits several staged batches as one atomic write and one fsync: all become durable together, or all stay staged for a retry. Each batch keeps its reserved sequence, and a crash never leaves half the group visible.
20	- `(*Log).Read(seq uint64) ([][]byte, error)` returns one committed batch, located directly through the persistent segment-level index (adopted from `index.idx` or rebuilt from the segment files on open).
21	- `(*Log).Scan(from uint64, fn func(Batch) error) error` replays committed batches in order.
22	- `(*Log).Segments() []Segment` lists segments with their first and last sequence.
23	- `type Options struct { SegmentBytes int; Sync bool }`.
24	- `log.ErrNotCommitted`, `log.ErrCorruptSegment`, `log.ErrUnknownBatch`, `log.ErrInvalidOptions`, `log.ErrSyncFailed` error values.
25	
26	## Tests
27	
28	    go test ./...
29	
30	## Limits
31	
32	Single writer; concurrent appends are not serialised.
33	Records are opaque bytes.
34	No compaction and no replication.

# batch-commit-log

Append only commit log that groups records into durable segments, so a writer publishes a batch atomically and a reader replays exactly the batches that were committed.

## Requirements

Go 1.22 or newer. Standard library only.

## Build

    go build ./...
    go run ./cmd/logctl --dir <path> stat

## Public interface

`log.Open(dir string, opts Options) (*Log, error)` opens the log directory. The committed set is taken from a persistent index sidecar (`index.idx`) when it can be adopted incrementally; if it is missing, truncated, version-mismatched, checksum-bad or contradictory to the segments, Open rebuilds it from the segment files, so the index is pure cache and opening a grown log no longer decodes every segment entry. A half-written tail of the last segment (crash mid-write) is discarded without error and its reserved sequence stays a permanent hole; any other inconsistency is `ErrCorruptSegment`.
- `(*Log).Append(records [][]byte) (Batch, error)` stages a batch.
- `(*Log).Commit(batch Batch) (uint64, error)` makes a batch durable and returns its sequence. The segment entry is synced first, then one index sidecar record; with `Sync`, a failed fsync of either returns `ErrSyncFailed`, both files roll back and the batch stays staged for a retry that never duplicates the entry.

- `(*Log).Read(seq uint64) ([][]byte, error)` returns one committed batch, located directly through the persistent segment-level index (adopted from `index.idx` or rebuilt from the segment files on open).
- `(*Log).Scan(from uint64, fn func(Batch) error) error` replays committed batches in order.
- `(*Log).Segments() []Segment` lists segments with their first and last sequence.
- `type Options struct { SegmentBytes int; Sync bool }`.
- `log.ErrNotCommitted`, `log.ErrCorruptSegment`, `log.ErrUnknownBatch`, `log.ErrInvalidOptions`, `log.ErrSyncFailed` error values.

Single writer; concurrent appends are not serialised.
Records are opaque bytes.

# batch-commit-log

Append only commit log that groups records into durable segments, so a writer publishes a batch atomically and a reader replays exactly the batches that were committed.

## Requirements

Go 1.22 or newer. Standard library only.

## Build

    go build ./...
    go run ./cmd/logctl --dir <path> stat

## Public interface

`log.Open(dir string, opts Options) (*Log, error)` opens the log directory. The committed set is taken from a persistent index sidecar (`index.idx`) when it can be adopted incrementally; if it is missing, truncated, version-mismatched, checksum-bad or contradictory to the segments, Open rebuilds it from the segment files, so the index is pure cache and opening a grown log no longer decodes every segment entry. A half-written tail of the last segment (crash mid-write) is discarded without error and its reserved sequence stays a permanent hole; any other inconsistency is `ErrCorruptSegment`.
- `(*Log).Append(records [][]byte) (Batch, error)` stages a batch.
- `(*Log).Commit(batch Batch) (uint64, error)` makes a batch durable and returns its sequence. The segment entry is synced first, then one index sidecar record; with `Sync`, a failed fsync of either returns `ErrSyncFailed`, both files roll back and the batch stays staged for a retry that never duplicates the entry.
- `(*Log).CommitGroup(batches []Batch) ([]uint64, error)` commits several staged batches as one atomic write and one fsync: all become durable together, or all stay staged for a retry. Each batch keeps its reserved sequence, and a crash never leaves half the group visible.
- `(*Log).Read(seq uint64) ([][]byte, error)` returns one committed batch, located directly through the persistent segment-level index (adopted from `index.idx` or rebuilt from the segment files on open).
- `(*Log).Scan(from uint64, fn func(Batch) error) error` replays committed batches in order.
- `(*Log).Segments() []Segment` lists segments with their first and last sequence.
- `type Options struct { SegmentBytes int; Sync bool }`.
- `log.ErrNotCommitted`, `log.ErrCorruptSegment`, `log.ErrUnknownBatch`, `log.ErrInvalidOptions`, `log.ErrSyncFailed` error values.

## Tests

    go test ./...

## Limits

Single writer; concurrent appends are not serialised.
Records are opaque bytes.
No compaction and no replication.

# batch-commit-log

Append only commit log that groups records into durable segments, so a writer publishes a batch atomically and a reader replays exactly the batches that were committed.

## Requirements

Go 1.22 or newer. Standard library only.

## Build

    go build ./...
    go run ./cmd/logctl --dir <path> stat

## Public interface

`log.Open(dir string, opts Options) (*Log, error)` opens the log directory. A half-written tail of the last segment (crash mid-write) is discarded without error and its reserved sequence stays a permanent hole; any other inconsistency is `ErrCorruptSegment`.

A key already in use by a batch with different records returns `ErrBatchIDConflict`. An empty key, a key containing NUL, non-UTF-8 key or a key over 256 bytes returns `ErrInvalidBatchID`.
- `Batch.ID() string` returns the idempotency key, or an empty string for an anonymous batch staged with `Append`. A keyed batch keeps the same ID and records under `Scan` after commit and across reopens, and `Read` returns those identical records.
- `(*Log).Commit(batch Batch) (uint64, error)` makes a batch durable and returns its sequence. - `(*Log).CommitGroup(batches []Batch) ([]uint64, error)` commits several staged batches — anonymous, keyed, or a mix — as one atomic write and one fsync: all become durable together, or all stay staged for a retry. Each batch keeps its reserved sequence, and a crash never leaves half the group visible.

实现完成，全部测试通过（58 个用例，含原有全部回归），`go build`/`go vet`/`gofmt` 干净。

## 实现概要

**公开 API（log.go）**
- 新增 `AppendIdempotent(key string, records [][]byte) (Batch, error)` 和 `Batch.ID() string`；匿名批次 `ID()` 返回 `""`。
- 新增错误 `ErrBatchIDConflict`、`ErrInvalidBatchID`。
- key 校验：非空、≤256 字节、合法 UTF-8、无 NUL。
- 去重逻辑：同 key 且记录长度/顺序/字节完全一致时，staged 返回同一批、committed 返回同一 `Seq`/`ID`（不预留序号、不写盘），重复 `Commit` 返回 `ErrUnknownBatch`；内容不同返回冲突。committed 去重的磁盘读取放在写锁之外（与 Read 一致）。
- `Commit`/`CommitGroup` 保持原子可见、预留顺序、fsync 失败双文件回滚且批次仍 staged；组提交可混匿名与带 key 批次。

**磁盘编码（segment.go，不新增文件）**
- 新增 `BCLK`（带 key 单批，seq+klen+key+records）和 `BCLM`（混合组，每成员 1 字节 flag + 可选 klen/key）；匿名批次仍用 `BCL1`/`BCLG`，绝不推断旧批次的 key。
- 解析器处理新帧；带 key 的半条尾记录按尾截断处理、序号成永久空洞，**key 不注册**，故同 key 重试建立新批次。

**索引（index.go）**
- sidecar 升到 v2：每成员 1 字节 flags + 可选 key，额外一位标记 BCLK body 布局。v1 sidecar 因版本不符触发整段重建，key 从段文件恢复。
- 采纳校验按段自身平铺逐成员核对 flag/key/seq，并拒绝重复 key（属篡改）；重建路径与快照同样校验 key 唯一性。

**验收测试（idempotent_test.go / idempotent_internal_test.go）**
覆盖同 key staged/committed 重试、记录冲突、非法 key、单批与混合组、段/索引 fsync 失败重试、重开去重、sidecar 缺失/截断/v1 降级重建、带 key 尾截断（单批与混合组）忘记 key、段篡改与 sidecar key 篡改、空批次/256 字节边界/分段滚动。错误仅为 `ErrBatchIDConflict`、`ErrInvalidBatchID`、`ErrUnknownBatch` 及既有恢复错误；目录内仍只有 `*.seg` 与 `index.idx`。
